To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the airway microbiome is different in asthmatics compared to healthy children, and that the microbiome is associated with the host immune response.
the microbiome is functionally distinct in asthmatics compared with non-asthmatics, and that the microbiome influences the host inflammatory and immune response.
we have shown for the first time that the microbiome and host transcriptome are differentially expressed in pediatric asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of airway microbiomes and its association to host-microbe interaction during health and disease.
the development of an integrative approach to study the functional characteristics of microbiomes and their relationship with the host.
the simultaneous analysis of host and microbial transcriptomes to identify host-microbe interaction mechanisms during health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbiome is a major determinant of the host immune response during asthma.

the microbiome is a complex ecosystem with a high degree of functional diversity that interacts with the host immune system in a way that may be related to the onset and/or progression of pediatric asthma.
the nasal microbiome of asthmatic children is functionally different from the microbiome of healthy children, and that these differences are associated with host immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of host and microbial functions differentially activated in asthmatic children compared to non-asthmatics, and that these functions are related to each other.
asthma is associated with changes in both the host and microbiome transcriptomes, and that the two interact with each other in a complex manner.
we were able to simultaneously profile the host and microbial functional characteristics of asthmatic and healthy children, and identify host-microbe associations that may contribute to disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive understanding of the airway microbial ecology in health and disease requires the integration of host and microbial functions.

a comprehensive analysis of the host-microbe transcriptome can be used to identify host and microbial functions that contribute to the development and maintenance of disease, and can be used to guide the design of future microbiome-based therapies.

simultaneous analysis of host-microbiota interactions from the same HTS experiment can be used to identify associations between microbiota characteristics and host responses, while accounting for the variation in clinical metadata.
